intent: One dark, monochrome text field for an email address. The label rests inside the field and, once focused or filled, rises onto the top hairline while the border opens a notch around it. Error and success text cross-fade in place of the helper, and a success tick draws itself in the trailing slot. Built with React 19, Tailwind CSS v4 and motion/react, with lucide-react for the mail glyph.

stack.styling: Tailwind CSS v4 (@container on the root, arbitrary values, one namespaced style block for the notch mask)
stack.animation: motion/react (animate for the notch edges and the label, AnimatePresence mode popLayout for messages, pathLength for the tick, useInView for the first reveal)

layout.root: @container block, max-width 420px, full width below; helper row sits 10px under the field
layout.field: 56px tall (md) or 64px (lg), border-radius 12px, position relative; surface layer, masked border layer, label, prefix, input, suffix stacked in that order
layout.padding: 16px horizontal (md), 18px (lg); leading slot 16px icon plus 10px gap when prefix is on; trailing slot 26px for suffix or the success tick
layout.helperRow: flex, items start, gap 16px; message left (min-width 0, flex 1), counter right and shrink-0; both inset by the field padding
layout.collapse: the label and text keep their offsets at every width; the field never shrinks below 280px

typography.input: sans, 16px (md) or 18px (lg), so iOS does not zoom
typography.label: sans, 15px (md) or 17px (lg), line box 20px; floated state is the same element scaled to 0.76 from the left centre
typography.message: sans 13px, leading 1.45; 13.5px from the @sm container breakpoint

color.usage: error colours only on the border, the message and the label in the error state; success colours only on the border, the message and the tick; everything else monochrome

motion.rise: label y and scale and notch edges share 320ms ease-out [0.22, 1, 0.36, 1]; notch edges write --fl-nl and --fl-nr imperatively from animate onUpdate, interruptible from the current position
motion.messages: popLayout cross-fade: enter from y 6px and blur 3px, exit to y -6px and blur 3px, 260ms ease-out
motion.tick: scale 0.8 to 1 with opacity over 240ms; path pathLength 0 to 1 over 420ms, 100ms delay
motion.reveal: once at 30% in view: the block rises 10px from blur 6px over 600ms
motion.reducedMotion: opacity changes at 150ms only, notch set instantly, tick drawn complete, no blur or offset

responsive.all: fluid to 420px; the field and helper row share one container; touch targets stay the full field height (56px or 64px)
responsive.widths: designed at 320, 390, 768 and 1440px; the label, notch and counter never overflow the field
responsive.touch: the whole field is the hit target, not the label; tapping the label focuses the input

accessibility: native input type email with inputMode email and autoComplete email; spellCheck off
label associated with htmlFor; the label is pointer-events none so taps reach the input
aria-invalid true in the error state; aria-describedby points at the message container
message container aria-live polite, so the error and success copy is announced once per change
disabled uses the native disabled attribute and dims the field to 42% opacity with cursor not-allowed
decorative layers, the mail glyph and the tick are aria-hidden
focus is shown on the field with a 2px ring; text inputs always show focus, so the ring is not limited to keyboard use

content.label: Work email
content.helper: We’ll send receipts and invoices here.
content.counter: Max 40 at rest, then 32 / 40 from 80% of the limit

avoid: a filled background behind the label, or a Material-style underline field
a glow, gradient or coloured fill on focus
a red warning triangle or a shake animation on error
the label jumping between positions instead of rising along one path
a live counter before 80% of the limit
a success tick that fades in rather than drawing
layout shift when the message changes or the label rises
blur or opacity on the input text itself
emoji or decorative sparkles anywhere in the field
per-frame React state for the notch edges
